linear-algebra.q: Two states satisfy ⟨u|v⟩ = 0. What does that tell you?
options: They are orthogonal — perfectly distinguishable by some measurement
They differ only by a global phase
linear-algebra.why: A zero inner product means orthogonality, and orthogonal states can be distinguished with certainty by measuring in a basis that contains them.

linear-algebra.q: The eigenvalues of a Hermitian operator are always…
linear-algebra.why: Hermitian operators have real eigenvalues — that is why observables are Hermitian. Only special ones (like the Paulis) have eigenvalues ±1.

complex-numbers-dirac-notation.q: How is the bra ⟨ψ| related to the ket |ψ⟩?
options: It is the same vector written backwards
It is the complex conjugate of each amplitude, kept as a column
complex-numbers-dirac-notation.why: ⟨ψ| = (|ψ⟩)† — transpose the column into a row and complex-conjugate each amplitude.

complex-numbers-dirac-notation.q: How do |ψ⟩ and e^{iθ}|ψ⟩ differ physically?
options: Not at all — a global phase is unobservable
They differ only when θ = π
complex-numbers-dirac-notation.why: All probabilities are |amplitude|², so a global phase cancels in every prediction. Only relative phases between components matter.

quantum-mechanics-basics.q: What does measuring a normalized qubit α|0⟩ + β|1⟩ in the Z basis do?
options: Reads out α and β without disturbance
Returns 0 or 1 with probabilities |α|² or |β|² and updates to that basis state
Rotates it by a random angle
quantum-mechanics-basics.why: The projectors |0⟩⟨0| and |1⟩⟨1| give Born probabilities |α|² and |β|². Conditional on the outcome, the normalized post-measurement state is |0⟩ or |1⟩; an input already in that eigenstate is unchanged.

quantum-mechanics-basics.q: Why can't an error-correcting code simply measure each data qubit in the computational basis to locate errors?
options: Those outcomes reveal logical information and generally dephase the encoded state
Errors are too small to see
quantum-mechanics-basics.why: Direct basis measurements generally reveal which logical components were present and dephase their superposition. QEC instead measures commuting parity checks through ancillas, extracting syndrome information without resolving the logical amplitudes.

qubits-pauli-operators.q: What is the algebraic relation between Pauli X and Z on the same qubit?
options: They are equal up to phase
They are inverses of each other
qubits-pauli-operators.why: XZ = −ZX. This anticommutation is the engine of QEC: a stabilizer flips sign exactly when an error anticommutes with it.

qubits-pauli-operators.q: Up to phase, the Pauli Y equals…
qubits-pauli-operators.why: Y = iXZ — a bit flip and a phase flip together. That is why a Y error triggers both X-type and Z-type stabilizers.

quantum-gates-circuits.q: An X error hits the control qubit just before a CNOT. What comes out?
options: X on both control and target
quantum-gates-circuits.why: CNOT copies X errors from control to target (and Z errors from target to control). Error propagation through CNOTs is why circuit design matters for fault tolerance.

quantum-gates-circuits.q: What does the Hadamard gate do to |0⟩?
quantum-gates-circuits.why: H exchanges the Z and X bases: |0⟩ ↔ |+⟩, |1⟩ ↔ |−⟩. It is how circuits switch between measuring Z-type and X-type information.

classical-error-correction.q: The 3-bit repetition code (0→000, 1→111) can correct how many bit flips?
classical-error-correction.why: Majority vote fixes any single flip. Two flips fool the vote — the codewords are distance 3 apart, and a distance-d code corrects ⌊(d−1)/2⌋ errors.

classical-error-correction.q: What does a parity check on a set of bits reveal?
options: Whether an even or odd number of those bits flipped
classical-error-correction.why: A parity check exposes only the XOR of the set — error information without reading the data. Stabilizer measurements are the quantum version of exactly this idea.

stabilizer-formalism.q: S is a stabilizer of |ψ⟩. What equation holds?
stabilizer-formalism.why: A stabilizer leaves the state exactly unchanged, eigenvalue +1. An error that anticommutes with S flips the measured value to −1 — that flip is the syndrome.

stabilizer-formalism.q: A stabilizer code on n physical qubits encoding k logical qubits has how many independent stabilizer generators?
stabilizer-formalism.why: Each independent generator halves the space; n − k generators leave 2^k dimensions — the logical subspace. The surface code: n = d², k = 1, so d²−1 stabilizers.

quantum-codes-basics.q: In the [[n, k, d]] notation, what is d?
options: The minimum weight of an undetectable logical error
quantum-codes-basics.why: d (code distance) is the smallest number of physical errors that can silently implement a logical operation. It sets how many errors are correctable: ⌊(d−1)/2⌋.

quantum-codes-basics.q: A CSS code is built from…
options: Two classical linear codes, one for X checks and one for Z checks
A single quantum code repeated twice
quantum-codes-basics.why: Calderbank–Shor–Steane codes import classical coding theory twice over: one classical code handles bit flips, another handles phase flips. The surface code is CSS.

fault-tolerance-thresholds.q: Under a threshold theorem's stated noise, locality, and gadget assumptions, what follows below p_th?
options: Logical error can be suppressed arbitrarily by increasing encoded overhead
fault-tolerance-thresholds.why: A threshold theorem is conditional: for the declared fault model and construction, sufficiently low fault strength permits arbitrary target accuracy with growing overhead. Above the fitted crossover, increasing distance no longer guarantees suppression; it is not a universal claim that every larger instance must be worse.

options: A single component fault can cause at most a correctable amount of damage
fault-tolerance-thresholds.why: The circuits that extract syndromes are themselves noisy, so they must be designed to keep one fault from spreading into an uncorrectable error — via gate ordering, flags, and repetition.

topological-order-anyons.q: In the ideal anyon model, what fixes the encoded action of an adiabatic braid?
options: Every microscopic wiggle of a homotopic path
The braid class of the world-lines, provided separation and the gap are maintained
topological-order-anyons.why: The ideal logical representation depends on braid class. A physical code-deformation schedule must still preserve distance and control faults; timing, geometry, and decoding determine its error rate and overhead.

topological-order-anyons.q: For the ideal toric-code Hamiltonian on a closed orientable surface, what controls the ground-space degeneracy?
topological-order-anyons.why: The ideal toric code has one ground state on a sphere and four on a torus. Ground states are locally indistinguishable in the ideal model, but a finite 2D code is not immune to noise and still needs active correction.

toric-code.q: How many logical qubits does the toric code on a torus encode?
toric-code.why: A torus has two independent non-contractible loops, giving two anticommuting logical operator pairs — two logical qubits, regardless of lattice size.

toric-code.q: The e and m excitations of the toric code appear at…
options: Violated vertex (star) and plaquette stabilizers — the endpoints of error strings
The corners of the lattice only
toric-code.why: Z-error strings end on violated stars (e anyons), X-error strings on violated plaquettes (m anyons). Errors make particle pairs; decoding means re-annihilating them correctly.

surface-code.q: Why is the surface code widely studied for hardware?
options: It needs the fewest qubits of every code
It combines local 2D checks with mature decoders and relatively high thresholds in common circuit models
It corrects unlimited errors at any rate
surface-code.why: Local connectivity and a developed circuit/decoder toolbox fit several hardware platforms. Its threshold and overhead are model-dependent, and other codes can win on rate, connectivity, or noise matching.

surface-code.q: A standard rotated surface-code patch of distance d uses how many data qubits?
surface-code.why: The common rotated one-logical-qubit layout uses d² data qubits, versus d²+(d−1)² in the corresponding unrotated layout—roughly half asymptotically. Ancilla counts and boundary check weights depend on the extraction layout.

syndrome-extraction-circuits.q: How does an ancilla measure a commuting stabilizer without resolving the logical amplitudes?
options: It swaps with a data qubit
An ordered entangling circuit maps the check parity to the ancilla, which is then measured
It measures every data qubit separately
syndrome-extraction-circuits.why: For example, a Z check uses |0⟩ with data-to-ancilla CNOTs and Z readout; an X check uses |+⟩ with ancilla-to-data CNOTs and X readout. The circuit measures the joint eigenspace rather than each data value.

syndrome-extraction-circuits.q: Why does the ordering of entangling gates in a stabilizer measurement matter?
options: It always changes the intended check
It controls how ancilla faults propagate into hook errors and therefore can change circuit distance
syndrome-extraction-circuits.why: A mid-circuit ancilla fault can spread to multiple data qubits. Whether that pattern is dangerous depends on patch geometry and logical orientation; a validated schedule preserves the intended distance, rather than being universally 'harmless' or exactly halving it.

decoding-mwpm.q: In a graphlike repeated-measurement model, what does MWPM pair?
options: Detection events or permitted boundaries, minimizing a specified total edge weight
decoding-mwpm.why: With noisy repeated checks, appropriate parity changes define space-time detection events. MWPM exactly minimizes its graph objective; this is only a proxy for full maximum likelihood when degeneracy, correlations, leakage, or hypergraph faults matter.

decoding-mwpm.q: When does a chosen correction cause a logical failure in an ideal topological decoding picture?
options: When error plus correction belongs to a nontrivial logical homology class
Whenever more than one defect appears
decoding-mwpm.why: A correction can return the state to the codespace yet differ from the true error by a silent logical operator. Zero syndrome therefore does not certify success, and with noisy extraction unresolved detector events also depend on protocol boundaries.

defects-braiding.q: In defect-based computation, what is a 'hole'?
options: A manufacturing defect in the chip
A region where stabilizer measurements are switched off, creating a movable logical qubit
defects-braiding.why: Disabling stabilizers punches a hole whose boundary hosts a new logical degree of freedom. Moving and braiding holes around each other enacts logical gates.

defects-braiding.q: Why do many planar surface-code studies prefer lattice surgery to defect braiding?
options: For the analyzed layouts, compact patch-parity measurements reduce routing or space-time cost
defects-braiding.why: Large separated defects and long deformation schedules can be expensive. Lattice surgery lowers cost in many planar architectures, but the comparison depends on connectivity, logical operation, code distance, and routing assumptions.

lattice-surgery.q: What does merging two surface-code patches along a boundary do?
options: Measures a joint logical operator (e.g. Z⊗Z)
Copies one qubit onto the other
lattice-surgery.why: The merged patch's new stabilizers multiply up to the joint logical Z⊗Z (or X⊗X), measuring it fault-tolerantly. Merge–split sequences build CNOTs and any Pauli-product measurement.

lattice-surgery.q: Why is lattice surgery widely used in surface-code architecture studies?
options: It expresses joint logical-Pauli measurements with local planar boundary checks and exposes routing/scheduling tradeoffs
lattice-surgery.why: Local planar checks fit common layouts and make occupancy and timing explicit. A full CNOT still needs an ancilla, two joint parities, final readout, and frame updates; relative cost remains architecture-dependent.

cluster-states-mbqc.q: How does measurement-based quantum computation compute?
options: By unitary gates applied in sequence
By adaptive single-qubit measurements consuming a pre-entangled cluster state
By cooling to the ground state
cluster-states-mbqc.why: All entanglement is prepared up front; each measurement steers the remaining state, with later bases adapted to earlier outcomes.

cluster-states-mbqc.q: What is the precise connection between topological MBQC and surface-code histories?
options: Specific RHG and foliated cluster constructions encode correlation surfaces corresponding to scheduled topological-code histories
MBQC removes the need for error correction
cluster-states-mbqc.why: The correspondence is construction-specific, not an identity for every 3D cluster state. Universal MBQC also needs adaptive non-Pauli measurements or equivalent injected magic resources beyond a Pauli-only stabilizer layer.

magic-states-distillation.q: Why do standard surface-code architectures use magic resources for T?
options: Because the surface code has no transversal T; consuming |A⟩ = T|+⟩ in a Clifford-and-measurement gadget can enact T
magic-states-distillation.why: Eastin-Knill forbids a universal transversal set under its assumptions, while surface-code T is commonly supplied by injection. Logical Cliffords are realized by tracking, surgery, deformation, or related code-dependent methods—not simply declared free.

magic-states-distillation.q: What is the leading accepted-output error of ideal 15-to-1 Bravyi-Kitaev distillation for independent small input error p?
magic-states-distillation.why: The ideal protocol's accepted marginal output error is cubic, 35p³ + O(p⁴). Acceptance probability, retries, output correlations, logical circuit faults, routing, and physical space-time cost are separate quantities.

flag-fault-tolerance.q: What does a flag outcome report in a validated extraction circuit?
options: The exact microscopic location of every fault
That the outcome pattern is consistent with a fault class that may have propagated dangerously
The end of any syndrome round
flag-fault-tolerance.why: Under the circuit's stated fault model, dangerous faults must produce a flag or a distinguishing syndrome. A flag narrows the allowed correlated-error set; it does not precisely identify every physical fault.

flag-fault-tolerance.q: What is a possible advantage of flag schemes?
options: Lower ancilla overhead than some verified-block constructions for selected codes and checks
flag-fault-tolerance.why: Some flag circuits use one or a few extra ancillas while meeting a proven fault-tolerance condition. The qubit saving and guarantee depend on the code, ordered circuit, distance, fault count, and recovery procedure.

options: A linear map, as a network of Z- and X-spiders that can be rewritten graphically
zx-calculus-basics.why: ZX rules are sound diagrammatic equations. Completeness requires an appropriate axiom set for the chosen fragment; the small introductory rules alone are not complete for every arbitrary qubit map.

zx-calculus-basics.q: Why can TQEC compilers use ZX-calculus?
options: Some lattice-surgery primitives have ZX representations, enabling semantics-preserving rewrites before layout
It guarantees removal of all non-Clifford gates
zx-calculus-basics.why: ZX is a useful intermediate representation linking logical maps to measurement structures. Rewrites preserve denotation, but whether they reduce T-count or space-time volume depends on the optimizer, input, and declared cost model.

advanced-decoding.q: What is a proved attraction of union-find decoding in its analyzed topological-code setting?
advanced-decoding.why: Its cluster-growth construction has favorable asymptotic complexity. Accuracy, threshold, latency, and practical speed relative to MWPM depend on the noise model, graph, implementation, and hardware.

advanced-decoding.q: Why do plain matching decoders lose accuracy on Y-type noise?
options: They decode X and Z syndromes independently, ignoring that Y errors correlate the two
Y errors have no syndrome endpoints
advanced-decoding.why: A Y error is a correlated X-and-Z event. Decoders that exploit the correlation (reweighting one matching using the other) measurably outperform independent decoding.

real-time-decoding-control.q: In a fixed-rate fluid queue, what happens when detector batches arrive at rate λ but the decoder serves at μ < λ?
options: The backlog repeatedly doubles despite fixed rates
The backlog grows approximately linearly at rate λ−μ while the deficit persists
Nothing if average latency is finite
real-time-decoding-control.why: A steady throughput deficit adds roughly the same unfinished work per unit time. Bursts and variable service can change queue statistics, but exponential growth does not follow from fixed arrival and service rates.

real-time-decoding-control.q: Why must a real-time decoder report both throughput and latency?
options: Throughput controls backlog, while some feed-forward decisions have separate deadlines
real-time-decoding-control.why: A pipeline can sustain a fast cycle stream while each result takes many cycles. Willow, for example, reported 63 μs average decoder latency while sustaining a 1.1 μs cycle stream; these are distinct measurements.

magic-state-cultivation.q: What sequence describes the original cultivation proposal?
options: Inject into a distance-3 triangular color code, cross-check/grow with postselection, then escape into a larger matchable encoding
magic-state-cultivation.why: The rough injected state initially has fault distance 1. Accepted cross-checks and growth raise protection; the escape/grafting circuit can add errors and must be included in full rejection and cost estimates.

magic-state-cultivation.q: How broad is the published resource evidence for cultivation?
options: It shows roughly order-of-magnitude qubit-round savings for selected baselines, intermediate target errors, and a specified depolarizing circuit model
It measures a hardware-independent fixed yield
magic-state-cultivation.why: The numerical advantage is scoped to the simulated pipeline, noise model, target regime, and comparison methods. It is not a universal recurrence, fixed yield, or hardware qubit count.

tqec-compilers-automation.q: What can a lattice-surgery compiler stage output?
options: A chip-ready pulse program by definition
A logical space-time layout or schedule candidate for patches, measurements, routing, and resources
tqec-compilers-automation.why: The candidate still needs architecture mapping, timing, decoder/control integration, distance validation, and an error budget before execution. A conceptual walkthrough or layout tool is not automatically a production compiler endpoint.

tqec-compilers-automation.q: In one Litinski-style representation, what happens to many Clifford operations?
options: They are deleted from the computation
They are propagated into a tracked frame, changing later Pauli-product measurements
tqec-compilers-automation.why: The logical effect remains accounted for through frame and measurement updates. This does not mean every architecture physically executes zero-cost Cliffords or that only T-count determines total space-time cost.

clifford-simulation-hybrid.q: What does the Gottesman–Knill theorem efficiently cover?
options: All circuits whose gates happen to be Clifford, with arbitrary input states
Stabilizer-state preparations, Clifford evolution, and Pauli measurements with classical feed-forward
clifford-simulation-hybrid.why: Efficient tableau tracking relies on stabilizer inputs and operations. Arbitrary non-stabilizer inputs fall outside the guarantee even if subsequent gates are Clifford.

clifford-simulation-hybrid.q: What does a hybrid quantum-circuit simulation establish?
options: The exact behavior of omitted hardware physics
Behavior of the represented circuit and noise model, with cost and uncertainty determined by the chosen method
clifford-simulation-hybrid.why: Stabilizer frames, decompositions, and factorization can enlarge the tractable regime. Finite sampling has uncertainty, exact trajectories are exact only for the modeled process, and leakage, drift, crosstalk, or other omitted effects remain outside the claim.

below-threshold-experiments.q: What did Google's 2024 Willow surface-code memory experiment establish?
options: Clear logical-error suppression across tested distances 3, 5, and 7 for its memory circuit and decoder
below-threshold-experiments.why: The 2022 work made a first larger-code comparison with modest average d=5 improvement over d=3. Willow added d=7 and reported a clear memory-scaling trend; it did not by itself demonstrate universal gates or an algorithm.

below-threshold-experiments.q: What convention did Willow use for the suppression factor Λ?
options: Λ = ε_L(d+2)/ε_L(d), so smaller is better
Λ = ε_L(d)/ε_L(d+2), so Λ > 1 means suppression
Λ is the physical-qubit lifetime ratio
below-threshold-experiments.why: Willow reported Λ = 2.14 ± 0.02 for the tested memories. The separate 2.4 ± 0.3 number compared encoded lifetime with the best constituent physical qubit; it was not Λ.
